messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT detected 2024-08-31 02:13 UTC - p95 latency spike on hosted inference API (us-west-2). Source: latency-slo-monitor. Severity: P1. Pager: sarah (oncall).

sarah (oncall): ack - I'm paged, joining. Any immediate customer impact?

incident-bot: Affected routes: /v1/completions (hosted), /v1/chat (hosted). Error rate increased marginally; latency p95 ~620ms. No data plane errors reported.

sarah (oncall): plan: 1) soft-rate-limit free-tier traffic to reduce load 2) partial brownout for long-context models 3) start draining problematic GPU pool in us-west-2 and shift traffic to us-east-1 if needed. @mike can you assess capacity for us-east-1?

mike (infra): seeing elevated GPU memory pressure on pool hosted-gpu-1 (us-west-2) + KV cache thrash. Us-east-1 has headroom but we'll need to spin up ~12 extra GPUs to absorb ~60% of traffic. Kicking off scale now.

ali (runtime): recommend immediate partial brownout: disable models with context >=4096 for hosted (keep for Dedicated/Private). Also route long-context requests to quantized 2048 variants. Will patch router.

sarah (oncall): do that now. Also enable soft quota throttles (per-tenant multiplier=0.8) for free-tier. Notify customers on status page.

jessica (eng-sre): I'm on it - updating runbook. I'll also set a traffic-shaping rule: cap RPS-per-tenant to 40 for free-tier while we stabilize.

mike (infra): starting drain of affected nodes. Running drain + reroute:
```
redwoodctl node drain --region us-west-2 --selector 'pool=hosted-gpu-1' --grace 60m
redwoodctl reroute traffic --from us-west-2 --to us-east-1 --percent 60
```

ali (runtime): applying router patch (will push in canary then global):
```
PATCH /v1/router/config
{
  'policy': 'latency-first',
  'overrides': [
    {'match': {'model_tags': ['long_context']}, 'action': 'route-us-east-1'},
    {'match': {'customer_tier': 'free'}, 'action': 'soft-rate-limit', 'limit': 0.8}
  ]
}
```

sarah (oncall): soft-rate-limit and router patch applied. Observing initial metrics - p95 dropping.

incident-bot: Metric update (02:18 UTC): p95 latency reduced from 620ms -> 340ms, error rate unchanged. GPU mem pressure decreasing on drained hosts.

customer-success-bot: Posting to status.redwood.ai: 'Degraded performance in us-west-2; mitigation in progress. Partial brownout for long-context hosted models; no customer data loss. Updates will follow.'

jessica (eng-sre): decision checkpoint: if p95 remains <400ms and error rate stable, keep partial brownout + soft-limits. If p95 >500ms or error rate >1% escalate to region failover (full drain). Ops, are we ready to reroute to GCP if AWS us-east-1 capacity saturates?

mike (infra): prepared. We have a warmed gcp-us-central pool as standby; provider reroute requires endpoint map flip + warming additional instances. Warming scripts running (estimate 12 min to warm extra capacity).

sarah (oncall): on-call handoff: I'll hand to ali in 20m. Notes for next oncall: applied soft-limit multiplier=0.8 for free-tier, router override routing long_context -> us-east-1, draining pool=hosted-gpu-1 (grace 60m), started scale in us-east-1. Escalation criteria: p95 >500ms OR error rate >1% -> execute full failover and provider reroute.

ali (runtime): ack, I'll take over at 02:33 UTC. I'll monitor p95, 95/99 and KV cache hit rates. If we need to do a partial brownout expansion, I'll disable streaming output for non-enterprise customers to reduce token churn.

sarah (oncall): quick mitigation command cheatsheet pushed to channel: 
```
# apply soft quota multiplier to free-tier
redwoodctl quota update --tier free --multiplier 0.8

# expand partial brownout - remove long-context models from hosted catalog
redwoodctl catalog set --region us-west-2 --remove-tag long_context --scope hosted
```

incident-bot: Update at 02:25 UTC - p95 340ms, error rate 0.12%, KV cache hit rate improving. Continue monitoring.

jessica (eng-sre): preparing post-incident customer impact assessment: list of affected customers (free-tier heavy users), duration of brownout, mitigation steps, and recommended follow-ups (increase cache, review model quantization for long-context).

mike (infra): drain progressed to 40% nodes drained; traffic rerouted ~60% to us-east-1. No failed pods.

ali (runtime): decided to keep streaming feature enabled for enterprise only (disabled for free/prod non-dedicated). This reduced per-token P99 spikes.

sarah (oncall): metrics look stable for 12 minutes. Holding partial brownout. If stable for 30m we'll start recovery steps (re-enable long-context models gradually and remove soft-limits).

incident-bot: 02:30 UTC - incident state: Mitigated (partial brownout + soft-limits). Postmortem owner assigned: jessica (eng-sre).

customer-success-bot: Status page updated: 'Mitigation in place. Services returning to normal. We will follow up with a post-incident report.'

jessica (eng-sre): assigning follow-ups: 1) Runtime: analyze KV cache misses and patch prefetch policy 2) Infra: investigate memory GC on hosted-gpu-1 pool 3) Product: evaluate long-context model usage patterns and pricing impacts of brownouts.

sarah (oncall): handing off to ali now. Leaving full notes above. If anything regresses ping me.

ali (runtime): taking over. I'll keep monitoring for 1hr and then mark incident closed if stable.

mike (infra): final note - we'll schedule a deeper maintenance window to repro and fix memory thrash.

jessica (eng-sre): postmortem ETA 48h. Thanks everyone for fast mitigation. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Thread archived after mitigation.
